relations.statement: If c(k) <= C for all k, p(k) >= 0 and p(k+1) <= c(k)*p(k)^2, then p(k) is bounded by an explicit level bound in C and p(0).
relations.hypotheses: hC: forall k, c k <= C; hp: forall k, 0 <= p k; hrec: forall k, p(k+1) <= c k * p k ^2

relations.statement: With D>0, p0>=0, D*p0 <= 1/2 and L <= eps*D*2^(2^k), we get L*p0-style bound L*(level error) <= eps.

lemmas.statement: Conditional viability: under g<1, kappa>0, supply r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa), c(k)<=C, max(C,1)*p(0)<1 and the level recurrence when the backlog is bounded, the backlog is bounded and for all L>=0, eps>0 some level k has L*p(k)<=eps.

lemmas.statement: Explicit version: with max(C,1)*p(0) <= 1/2, any k with L <= eps*max(C,1)*2^(2^k) gives L*p(k) <= eps.

lemmas.statement: Toy instance showing the hypotheses are jointly satisfiable on declared numbers (BacklogBounded 1 (1/2) (1*2) 0 and level error with conc 4 (1/10)).

near_misses.claim: Drop the max(C,1)*p(0) < 1 threshold: double-exponential decay of p(k) still holds.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: If C*p(0) >= 1 the recurrence p(k+1) <= C*p(k)^2 permits p(k) to be non-decreasing, so L*p(k) <= eps can fail.

near_misses.claim: Supply rate r below lam/((1-g)*kappa) still gives a bounded backlog.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The backlog bound requires r >= lam/((1-g)*kappa); below it, repair cannot keep up and the recurrence hypothesis is not triggered.
